title: Money & currency
body: Japanese Yen (¥/JPY). Card acceptance keeps broadening at tourist-facing venues, but this trip's actual food priorities skew cash-heavy — yatai stalls are ~90% cash-only, and plenty of ramen counters and markets are too. Withdraw at 7-Eleven ATMs (Seven Bank), which reliably accept foreign cards 24/7. Check the current JPY/USD rate before you go — the figures below assume a rough ≈¥150/$1, unconfirmed against a live rate this pass.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Rough per-person USD estimates for a mid-to-high, comfortable ($150–300/day target) trip — toggle for trip-total or per-person. The Zao Onsen ryokan night is the one deliberate splurge; lodging otherwise is business-hotel-level to keep the daily average sane. Gaming/anime shopping is wide open by nature — treat that line as a floor, not a ceiling. All figures are ≈ estimates, not fixed quotes — confirm as you book.

items.label: Lodging, per night
items.note: Business-hotel-level in Fukuoka/Sapporo/Sendai — twin rooms near the station or entertainment district run roughly this range. (⚠ a general estimate, not a specific booked rate.)

items.label: Zao Onsen ryokan — 1 night, 2 meals incl.
items.note: Miyamaso Takamiya, per person, kaiseki dinner + breakfast included — Japanese ryokan pricing is per-person, not per-room. Aggregator-sourced (≈$250/person); the ryokan's own site pushes to its booking system rather than posting a rate, so get the real quote when you book. This is the trip's one explicit splurge — the belated-birthday night.

items.label: Food & drink, per day
items.note: Ramen ≈$8–12/bowl, yatai ≈$20–30/evening for a few stalls, motsunabe/mentaiko sit-down dinners and the birthday jingisukan dinner push individual days well past the average. (⚠ a general estimate, not a single sourced figure.)

items.label: Local transport, per day
items.note: City subway/bus fares most days; occasional taxi for late nights or awkward connections (e.g. Zao Onsen, Jozankei).

items.label: Domestic flights (Tokyo→Fukuoka→Sapporo→Sendai)
items.note: Three domestic legs, aggregator fare ranges (≈$90 + ≈$60 + ≈$80, one-way each) plus the Sendai→Tokyo Hayabusa Shinkansen (≈¥11,410 ≈$75) at the end. None of these are airline-quoted — re-check nearer to booking.

items.label: Regional rail passes (JR Kyushu + JR East–South Hokkaido, if worth it)
items.note: JR Kyushu Northern Pass (5-day, ¥17,000 ≈$113) and/or JR East–South Hokkaido Rail Pass (6-day, ¥40,000 ≈$266) — compare against point-to-point tickets for the actual planned routes before buying; regional passes pay off on genuinely regional itineraries like this one, per repeated traveler reports, but only if the specific days used justify the price.

items.label: Sights & activities, per day
items.note: Ropeway fares (Mt. Moiwa, Zao), the Matsushima boat cruise, and similar — many days (Naruko Gorge, Jigokudani, yatai-hopping) cost nothing to just walk through.

items.label: eSIM / data
items.note: Ubigi unlimited/30-day ≈$65 (two 30-day cycles needed to cover ~26 days); the 20GB/30-day tier is ≈$19 if data use is lighter than expected.

items.label: Luggage forwarding (Yamato Ta-Q-Bin)
items.note: ≈$11–25 per suitcase per shipment — budget two shipments (e.g. sending bags ahead of the Zao Onsen overnight, and again before the final Tokyo departure).

items.label: Gaming/anime shopping
items.note: Wide open by design — this is the discretionary line for Mandarake/Animate/gacha runs across Fukuoka, Sapporo and Sendai. Anything bought Nov 1 onward uses the new refund-at-departure tax-free process (see Plan tab) rather than the instant discount.

items.label: Flights — international round trip
items.note: Rough transpacific range into/out of Tokyo (HND/NRT) — swings hugely on carrier, dates, and how far ahead you book. Check ANA Mileage Club / United MileagePlus (Star Alliance) or American AAdvantage on JAL (oneworld) if using miles.
